sections.title: Sound of C
paragraphs: The letter (C) /s/ has the name (C) /s/. Its primary sound is the sound /k/, heard in the word (cat) /kæt/, which means cat. This letter produces two different sounds in spoken English.

sections.title: How to say C
paragraphs: To make the first sound, lift the back of your tongue against the roof of your mouth. Release the air suddenly without using your voice. For the second sound, bring your tongue tip close to your upper gum. Push air smoothly through the narrow opening without using your voice. You can feel cool air on your hand.

sections.title: Spelling of C
paragraphs: This letter makes the sound /k/ before the vowels a, o, u, or before consonants, as in (cup) /kʌp/. It makes the sound /s/ when it stands directly before the letters e, i, or y, as in (cent) /sɛnt/.

sections.title: Pitfalls with C
paragraphs: A common mistake is using the wrong sound before different vowels. Remember not to use the sound /k/ before the letters e, i, or y. Do not use your voice on either sound, because both are completely voiceless.
